cues.title: On the CCC road

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: Part of the CCC route, here.

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: So this is the CCC road up to Dean’s Mountain?

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: It is.

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: It doesn't look too much different when my grandparents brought me out here. Except it's got rock on it, it didn't have rock then.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

cues.title: Reading the forest

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: They're filling [forested] holes. See how much opening you get in these groves? Guess that's what those birds need to land in.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

cues.title: Remembering the CCC crews

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: It still amazes me, when they built their camps, they swore they were not going to lose a single day's work, ever. And they didn't. They carried that out for seven years. They never lost a day's work, and they took Sunday off. And they never killed a man. Here are all these 18, 19 year-old boys,

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: no hard hats, no canopies for the tractors, using explosives all the time, never killed a single kid.
lines.attributionNote: Continued from page 140; speaker inferred from the printed paragraph.

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: They got a lot done, too. It’s not a very big camp where we’re going.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

cues.title: Work and recollection

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: They broke all of today's industrial accident rules.

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: That's why they're still alive, I guess.

lines.speaker: Randy Wiest
lines.text: They focused on staying safe instead of being protected?

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Well I went around and interviewed three of them for my book, and I found all those three.

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: Kids from the city, too, they got some of them.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Scattered all around western Oregon, and Charleston, Brownsville, all these different places. Of course some went back home again. Some were from Missouri.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: Jerry, if you had to do it over, would you still have them convert the myrtle to fir, or would you tend to just leave the myrtle as it is?

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Well, we have so little of it that that was never really a question that we dealt with. We probably would have left it, since there's so little, but the mission was, originally, to try to grow pure Douglas fir on all the land that was available.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Of course, you had to try to harvest all the old-growth fir, get rid of it, ‘cause it wasn't growing, and get rid of all the alder, ‘cause it was worthless, and then get pure Douglas fir in all the rest. So you would eliminate maple -- of course, we had very little maple -- and myrtle, which was also very, very little.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: But we're living in this day and age where we're celebrating diversity of all kinds, so we probably would've been directed at an HCP [ESA Habitat Conservation Plan] to keep it.

cues.title: Toward the lookout

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: You all want to go down to the waterhole first?

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: Sure, and we got to come back this way too, don't we?

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: ‘Cause the waterhole's down that way and the lookout's down that way.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Well, you want to turn right here.

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: We'll get it on the way back.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

cues.title: Can we get there?

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: You intend to go up to Deans Mountain?

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: I don't know if we can get up there or not, but we can see the road from here.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: Probably a locked gate.

lines.speaker: Amber Ross
lines.text: Yeah, we've got a key, we can get up there.

cues.note: Timing is approximate for quiet or overlapping remarks.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: I haven't been up there for. . .well, I guess it's been forty years. And I know it's changed totally, but it's still there.

cues.title: A familiar landmark

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: Well that's one of the most historic places on the whole forest.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: It's the most historic. I said in my book –

lines.speaker: Amber Ross
lines.text: It’s clearcut now.

lines.speaker: Bob Zybach
lines.text: What's that?

lines.speaker: Amber Ross
lines.text: It's clear cut now.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: It's probably the only. . .

lines.speaker: David Gould
lines.text: We're here.

lines.speaker: Jerry Phillips
lines.text: . . . it's the only landmark most people know on the forest.
